info.name: QuickBite — Order Service
info.description: Folders match the modules in order-service/src/app/*. X-Region header is set per request. Idempotency-Key uses {{$randomUUID}}. Order public id is captured automatically by the 'Place order' tests.

request.description: Creates a Kashier session. Response includes `payment.redirectUrl` — open it in a browser to actually pay. Saves paymentRedirectUrl.

item.name: Order — Restaurant (owner)
item.description: Restaurant-side transitions. Driven by `owner` because owner bypasses `requireBranchAccess`. Manager/staff are also valid restaurant roles, but in the current code the JWT carries `branchIds` as strings (pg BIGINT) and the middleware compares with `.includes(Number(...))` — so non-owner members get a false-negative 403. Use owner for the happy path; manager/staff variants are kept below for negative-RBAC checks.

item.name: Accept order AS MANAGER (expected 403 — non-owner branchIds bug)

request.description: Sanity check. With the current middleware this fails 403 because the JWT carries branchIds as strings. Useful as a negative test until the middleware is fixed.
paymentId here is the transactions.id from a successful COD/online charge.
Public webhook. Real calls come from Kashier with a valid HMAC signature; this mock is for shape reference only — it WILL fail signature verification.
Idempotent. Wins the order via SETNX claim. Cancels offer to other candidates.

item.name: Mark DELIVERED (agent EG) — settles earnings + balance

request.description: Decrements the restaurant balance. Will fail if balance is below `amount`.

item.name: WebSocket (Socket.IO)
item.description:
Each request opens a raw WebSocket against the order-service socket.io engine.io endpoint:
  ws://localhost:4000/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket

Auth: the JWT is delivered via the `Cookie: access_token=...` header. The WS server's
`ws-auth.ts` reads either `handshake.auth.token` (only set by socket.io clients) or the
`access_token` cookie — query-string tokens are deliberately disabled.

How to use in Postman v10+:
  1. Login the relevant role first in the Auth folder so the role-scoped token is set.
  2. Open this request and click **Connect**.
  3. In the 'New Message' panel, change the message type to **Text** and send the
     Socket.IO protocol frames listed in each request's description.

Socket.IO v4 protocol cheat-sheet (engine.io packets + socket.io payload):
  '0'                                     ← server sends: engine.io OPEN  (auto)
  '40'                                    → send to upgrade to Socket.IO  (NAMESPACE CONNECT)
  '40{"sid":"..."}'                    ← server replies: CONNECT ack
  '2'  /  '3'                             heartbeat ping / pong (every 25s, auto by Postman)
  '42["subscribe","<channel>"]'        → send to subscribe to a permitted channel
  '42["<event>",<payload>]'             ← server broadcasts events with this shape

Channels per role (validated by `permittedChannels` on the server):
  customer:<userId>           — everyone gets their own
  restaurant:<restaurantId>   — restaurant_user (any role)
  branch:<branchId>           — restaurant_user with that branch in branchIds
  agent:<userId>              — delivery_agent

Expected server events (see TESTING_GUIDE.md §8):
  hello { allowedChannels: string[] }       — sent immediately after CONNECT
  subscribed { channel }                    — ack for your subscribe call
  order.created  ← branch:<id>              — fired on place (COD) / pay success (online)
  order.status_changed ← customer/branch    — every transition
  task.offered   ← agent:<id>               — assignment loop picked this agent
  task.assigned  ← agent:<winnerId>         — agent claimed the offer
  offer.cancelled ← agent:<loserIds>        — other candidate won

request.description:
After connect, send these frames in order (one per message):
  40
  42["subscribe","customer:{{customerUserId}}"]

Then place a COD order in the 'Order — Customer' folder — you'll see
  42["order.status_changed",{...}]  on every restaurant/agent transition.

After connect, send:
  40
  42["subscribe","restaurant:{{restaurantId}}"]
  42["subscribe","branch:{{branchEgId}}"]
  42["subscribe","branch:{{branchKsaId}}"]

Owner is in all branches by virtue of restaurantRole='owner'.
You'll see  42["order.created",{...}]  on branch:<id> whenever a customer places an order.

After connect, send:
  40
  42["subscribe","agent:{{agentEgUserId}}"]

Then in another tab: POST /agents/presence/online + place + accept + ready an order.
Within the assignment-tick window (~10s) you should see:
  42["task.offered",{...}]   ← offer arrived
  42["task.assigned",{...}]  ← (if you call /accept and win)
  42["offer.cancelled",{...}]  ← (if a different candidate wins)

Same as the EG agent, but for the KSA region.
  40
  42["subscribe","agent:{{agentKsaUserId}}"]

After connect, send:
  40
  42["subscribe","admin:alerts"]

Receives  42["assignment.exhausted",{orderId, attempts}]  when the assignment loop
gives up on an order after ASSIGNMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 3) tries.
